host: Apple M4, macOS 26.6.1, load 1-3 unless noted
question: WORKORDER O1: 2 of 9 benchmark runs read ~100 MB higher at idle. What is it?
answer: Where in dmx's idle cycle the reading falls. With dockerd up, the footprint sits at ~260 MB until the idle trim and sweep fire 30 s after the last activity (5 s tick, the host has the memory ~2 s later), drops to ~185-205 MB, and then creeps to ~210-225 MB as dockerd and containerd read some of their files back. The benchmark's fixed 35 s settle landed on either side of the trim.

one_run_timeline_footprint_mb.note: guest used 65-66 MB throughout; the difference is guest memory free but not yet returned

twelve_idle_runs_before_the_harness_chan.note: same VM state each run, 35 s settle; the first run's longer image pull pushed its reading past the trim

benchmark_with_the_window_sampled.note: scripts/benchmark.py now samples 35, 50, 65, 80 and 95 s; three runs

guest_compaction_tried_and_dropped.what: /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory from the idle sweep, through a new agent call, plus a 4 MB touch to wake free page reporting
guest_compaction_tried_and_dropped.why_it_looked_promising: compacting a VM in the pre-trim state took it from 258-270 MB to 173-197 MB, but that is the memory the trim and sweep return a few seconds later anyway
guest_compaction_tried_and_dropped.verdict: no gain, so the agent call and the sweep change were reverted; see also the first-boot unpack row of the same day

conclusion: No memory is lost and nothing in the product changed. The harness now records the whole idle window: idle_at_35s (what the old runs measured), idle_min (the floor the trim reaches) and idle (the steady state). Published comparison numbers quote the 35 s definition, so the steady state is ~20 MB higher than the 198 MB in README and benchmark.md.
